text: When dealing with text, standard pages and lines are used for practical reasons, basically as convenient units. Their use enables us to compare one text with another by volume, irrespective of the format. text: In the days of the typewriter, a standard page had 30 lines × 60 keystrokes = 1,800 characters. This definition is occasionally used to this day. Normally, however, the whole page is not filled with text, as paragraphs and headings take up considerable space. Today, a standard page is more commonly defined as having 1,650 or 1,500 characters, which is more realistic. According to the German copyright collecting society VG Wort, the standard page has 1,500 keystrokes. This is the definition that we follow.
